html:
Urartu was an Iron Age kingdom in the mountains around Lake Van, in the Armenian highlands of today's eastern Turkey, Armenia and northwest Iran. It lasted from the 800s to the 500s BCE; the map shows the area under the name from 1500 to 700 BCE.

Its capital was Tushpa, on a rock above Lake Van. Its kings built fortresses on hilltops, long irrigation canals and large storehouses for wine and grain, and they were skilled in bronze work. King Argishti I founded the fortress of Erebuni in 782 BCE, the origin of Yerevan. The Urartians spoke a language related to that of the Hurrians and wrote it in cuneiform.

Urartu was the great northern rival of Assyria, which attacked it many times; in 714 BCE Sargon II led a famous campaign against it. Urartu outlasted Assyria but fell in the early 500s BCE, probably to the Medes or Scythians. Its land became Armenia.
